messages.author: ff7d32384083b3d7
messages.subject: running CODEX with read depth as input
parts:
Hi Yuchao,

I'm wondering if I can use read depth (read count) data directly, instead of .bam files, as input to run CODEX. When I looked at the code, it looks like that all I need is to use read count data to replace Y from #2.3 part. Then I can skip the bam file part, but just run CODEX with a bed file and 'sampname' file, is that right? If you have scripts ready for that, I would really appreciate if you can share, Thanks!

Peng



##########################
# 2.3 Get raw read depth from the .bam files. Read lengths across all samples are also returned.
 coverageObj <- getcoverage(bambedObj, mapqthres = 20)
 Y <- coverageObj$Y; readlength <- coverageObj$readlength

> head(Y)
     [,1] [,2] [,3]
[1,]   16   21   15
[2,]   45   43   39
[3,]   16   33   24
[4,]   15   13   17
[5,]   13   16   12
[6,]  110  114   70

messages.author: 94ec915e8ce36448
messages.subject: Re: [codex_wes_cnv] running CODEX with read depth as input
parts:
Hi Peng,

Yes of course! If you have depth of coverage, just specify Y using that (make sure that the dimension is by CODEX's default, i.e., exons x samples). Then specify chr, sampname as a column vector of sample names. Then you can basically run the code below to generate ref and run QC, normalization, etc.

exomtarg <- read.table(bedFile, sep = "\t")
exomtarg <- exomtarg[exomtarg[, 1] == chr, ]
ref <- IRanges(start = exomtarg[, 2], end = exomtarg[, 3])
gc <- getgc(chr, ref)
mapp <- getmapp(chr, ref)

qcObj <- qc(Y, sampname, chr, ref, mapp, gc, cov_thresh = c(20, 4000), 
    length_thresh = c(20, 2000), mapp_thresh = 0.9, gc_thresh = c(20, 80))
Y_qc <- qcObj$Y_qc; sampname_qc <- qcObj$sampname_qc; gc_qc <- qcObj$gc_qc
mapp_qc <- qcObj$mapp_qc; ref_qc <- qcObj$ref_qc; qcmat <- qcObj$qcmat
write.table(qcmat, file = paste(projectname, '_', chr, '_qcmat', '.txt', sep=''),
            sep='\t', quote=FALSE, row.names=FALSE)

HI Yuchao,

when I tried using read count as input, I got the following error message, where there are "NA" count of exons filtered from extreme coverage, I tried different chromosomes and it always gave the same error, but using bam files as input for the same set of samples seemed to work fine, any ideas? thanks!

# with read count as input
> # 2.5 Take a sample-wise and exon-wise quality control procedure on the depth of coverage matrix.
>  qcObj <- qc(Y, sampname, chr, ref, mapp, gc, cov_thresh = c(20, 4000),

+  length_thresh = c(20, 2000), mapp_thresh = 0.9, gc_thresh = c(20, 80))
Excluded NA exons due to extreme coverage.
Excluded 58 exons due to extreme exonic length.
Excluded 51 exons due to extreme mappability.
Excluded 12 exons due to extreme GC content.
After taking union, excluded NA out of 3672 exons in QC.
Error: logical subscript contains NAs
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In FUN(newX[, i], ...) : integer overflow - use sum(as.numeric(.))
2: In FUN(newX[, i], ...) : integer overflow - use sum(as.numeric(.))

# with bam files as input
> qcObj <- qc(Y, sampname, chr, ref, mapp, gc, cov_thresh = c(20, 4000),

+  length_thresh = c(20, 2000), mapp_thresh = 0.9, gc_thresh = c(20, 80))
Excluded 146 exons due to extreme coverage.
Excluded 58 exons due to extreme exonic length.
Excluded 51 exons due to extreme mappability.
Excluded 12 exons due to extreme GC content.
After taking union, excluded 249 out of 3672 exons in QC.
